title: Progressive-fetch embeddings client with circuit-breaker, structured errors, and typed responses
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Our embeddings + reranking workloads are increasingly sensitive to tail latency and variability across large batched requests. Existing client pagination surfaces require callers to either fetch full pages or implement complex cursor rehydration for partial responses. We also lack a lightweight circuit-breaker and a consistent typed error taxonomy across Python and TypeScript SDKs, which complicates retry logic in downstream services.

Goal: Implement a progressive-fetch client pattern for embeddings that allows streaming/partial page consumption, add an adaptive client-side circuit-breaker tuned for per-model and per-route characteristics, and publish a stable structured error schema with TypeScript interfaces and Python TypedDicts. Deliverables should improve 95th/99th latency, reduce client-level retry storms, and make error handling ergonomics consistent across languages.

Non-goals: Changing server-side pagination cursor format, removing server SLO guarantees, or forcing breaking surface changes for existing customers unless explicitly gated behind a versioned flag.

Proposed changes:
- Client API: introduce EmbeddingsClient.list_embeddings(progressive=true|false, page_size=int, max_inflight= int) that returns:
  - TS: AsyncIterable<EmbeddingPage<TypedEmbedding>> where TypedEmbedding is a stable interface.
  - Python: AsyncIterator[TypedDict("Embedding", {...})] and a sync iterator helper.
- Progressive fetch semantics: client will emit partial pages as soon as a configurable threshold (e.g., 50% of page) is ready to reduce head-of-line blocking for long-running model calls. Caller can request to drain remaining items or cancel.
- Circuit-breaker: per-client configurable circuit breaker with three states (closed, open, half-open). Default thresholds: open when > 5% error rate over 1m window and average latency > 1.5x baseline; exponential backoff with jitter for probing. 
- Retry & backoff: distinguish retryable transient errors (network timeouts, 5xx service issues) from structured client errors (invalid args, rate-limit exceeded). Retries should respect progressive-fetch cancellation semantics.
- Error taxonomy & typed responses: publish ErrorCode enum (INVALID_REQUEST, RATE_LIMIT, SERVER_ERROR, MODEL_INVALID_SEQUENCE, KV_CACHE_MISS) and attach stable fields: code, message, retriable (bool), retry_after (seconds optional), docs_url, request_id. Provide TypeScript interfaces and Python TypedDicts in SDK packages.
- Observability: emit metrics for progressive-pages-emitted, progressive-page-latency_p50/p95/p99, circuit_breaker_state transitions, and retry_count by code.
- Backward compatibility: keep existing EmbeddingsClient.generate_embeddings(...) and paginated helpers but add a feature flag "progressive_fetch_v1" and a minor-version SDK release. Provide migration guide.

Why this matters: Many downstream reranking flows do early scoring and short-circuit on top-k; getting a fast partial page often yields lower end-to-end latency than waiting for full pages. The circuit-breaker prevents hotspot retry storms when a model variant degrades. Typed errors and responses simplify deterministic behavior for platform teams integrating into scoring pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: New progressive-fetch API available in Python and TS SDKs behind feature flag progressive_fetch_v1
Can stream/iterate partial pages and cancel remaining fetch in both languages
Circuit-breaker open/close metrics emitted and default thresholds documented
Structured Error schema published in SDK docs and surfaced as typed objects in TS and Python
E2E benchmark: 95th-percentile latency for a top-k rerank flow reduced by at least 15% on our internal benchmark for mixed small/large queries
No breaking changes to existing pagination helpers unless flag enabled; migration guide published
notes: Prototype PR (TS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 - progressive iterator + typed interfaces
Perf harness: internal benchmark suite at /bench/embeddings/progressive_fetch_v1 (run with --topk=50 --mix=heavy)
Spike notes: team experimented with 30%, 50%, 70% thresholds; 50% gave best latency/cost tradeoff for heterogeneous payloads
Related issues: ENG-61421 (kv-cache stabilization), ENG-61800 (retry strategy consolidation)
